source.source_project: A — richer teaching interface with handwritten dynamics

extraction_note: Files were generated from the five historical default model definitions. Only listed XML/comment corrections and a provenance comment were applied. No controller or handwritten physics was copied into the active application.

reference_sources.title: MuJoCo Modeling — solver parameters
reference_sources.use: Positive solref values express time constant and damping ratio. The chosen 0.02 1 is an explicit baseline, not a restitution conversion.

models.name: Cartpole balance
remaining_caveats: No feedback controller is embedded. A motor alone will not balance an unstable pole.
The sensor named pole_tip measures the pole body origin, not the geometric tip; rename or replace it with a site sensor before relying on that name.
The original JavaScript initial state and controller are not reproduced by this XML.
models.original_xml:
<mujoco model="cartpole_balance">
  <!-- Keep the pole upright using one actuator on the cart. -->
  <option gravity="0 0 -9.81"
          timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="0 2.4 3" dir="0 -1 -1" directional="true"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"
          rgba="0.35 0.37 0.32 1"/>

    <body name="cart" pos="0 0 0.18">
      <joint name="slide" type="slide" axis="1 0 0"
             damping="0.060" limited="true"
             range="-2.2 2.2"/>
      <geom name="cart" type="box" size="0.26 0.16 0.11"
            mass="1.00" rgba="0.86 0.84 0.74 1"/>

      <body name="pole" pos="0 0 0.11">
        <joint name="hinge" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
               damping="0.004"/>
        <geom name="pole" type="capsule"
              fromto="0 0 0 0 0 0.90"
              size="0.026" mass="0.22"
              rgba="0.93 0.51 0.27 1"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>

  <actuator>
    <motor name="drive" joint="slide" gear="1"
           ctrlrange="-20 20"/>
  </actuator>

  <sensor>
    <jointpos name="pole_angle" joint="hinge"/>
    <jointvel name="pole_velocity" joint="hinge"/>
    <framepos name="pole_tip" objtype="body" objname="pole"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>

models.name: Double pendulum

changes.reason: Move the anchor above the Z=0 plane; original gravity and link geometry already use Z as vertical.

remaining_caveats: No initial perturbation/keyframe is included; the default hanging pose may remain stationary.
MuJoCo joint coordinates are relative to each parent, whereas the historical handwritten equations used two absolute link angles.
These links have distributed capsule mass, unlike the point-mass idealization in the historical explanation.
models.original_xml:
<mujoco model="double_pendulum">
  <!-- Deterministic chaos from two coupled hinges. -->
  <option gravity="0 0 -9.81"
          timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="0 2 3" dir="0 -1 -1" directional="true"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"/>
    <body name="ceiling" pos="0 2.1 0">
      <geom name="anchor" type="box" size="0.16 0.05 0.16"
            mass="0.01" rgba="0.2 0.22 0.2 1"/>

      <body name="upper" pos="0 0 0">
        <joint name="shoulder" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
               damping="0.012"/>
        <geom name="upper_link" type="capsule"
              fromto="0 0 0 0 0 -0.72"
              size="0.024" mass="0.22"
              rgba="0.88 0.85 0.76 1"/>

        <body name="lower" pos="0 0 -0.72">
          <joint name="elbow" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
                 damping="0.012"/>
          <geom name="lower_link" type="capsule"
                fromto="0 0 0 0 0 -0.62"
                size="0.022" mass="0.18"
                rgba="0.93 0.51 0.27 1"/>
        </body>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>

  <sensor>
    <jointpos name="q1" joint="shoulder"/>
    <jointpos name="q2" joint="elbow"/>
    <jointvel name="q1_dot" joint="shoulder"/>
    <jointvel name="q2_dot" joint="elbow"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>

models.name: Driven pendulum

changes.reason: Move the anchor above the Z=0 plane; original gravity and link geometry already use Z as vertical.

remaining_caveats: No sinusoidal controller is embedded; the motor requires an external control signal.
No initial perturbation/keyframe is included; the default hanging pose may remain stationary.
models.original_xml:
<mujoco model="driven_pendulum">
  <!-- Torque input pumps energy into a single hinge. -->
  <option gravity="0 0 -9.81"
          timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="0 2 3" dir="0 -1 -1" directional="true"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"/>
    <body name="mount" pos="0 1.9 0">
      <geom name="bearing" type="cylinder" size="0.08 0.12"
            mass="0.05" rgba="0.22 0.24 0.22 1"/>

      <body name="link" pos="0 0 0">
        <joint name="hinge" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
               damping="0.045"/>
        <geom name="rod" type="capsule"
              fromto="0 0 0 0 0 -0.80"
              size="0.021" mass="0.02"
              rgba="0.88 0.85 0.76 1"/>
        <geom name="bob" type="sphere" pos="0 0 -0.80"
              size="0.105" mass="0.50"
              rgba="0.93 0.51 0.27 1"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>

  <actuator>
    <motor name="kick" joint="hinge" gear="1"
           ctrlrange="-4.2 4.2"/>
  </actuator>

  <sensor>
    <jointpos name="theta" joint="hinge"/>
    <jointvel name="theta_dot" joint="hinge"/>
    <actuatorpos name="drive_pos" actuator="kick"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>

models.name: Two-link arm
remaining_caveats: The two actuators are motors, not position servos. The original comment mentioning a servo describes an intended external controller.
The home keyframe is not automatically applied on load. Positive rotation about the given +Y axes moves the first link toward negative Z; inspect this keyframe against the floor before using it.
The historical handwritten arm dynamics and their displayed targets are not reconstructed by this MJCF.
models.original_xml:
<mujoco model="planar_arm">
  <!-- Serial manipulator with a compliant joint-space servo. -->
  <option gravity="0 0 -9.81"
          timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="1 3 3" dir="-1 -1 -1" directional="true"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"/>
    <geom name="pedestal" type="cylinder" pos="0 0 0.12"
          size="0.2 0.12" mass="0.5" rgba="0.2 0.22 0.2 1"/>

    <body name="upper" pos="0 0 0.28">
      <joint name="shoulder" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
             damping="0.18"/>
      <geom name="upper_link" type="capsule"
            fromto="0 0 0 1.05 0 0"
            size="0.07" mass="0.90"
            rgba="0.88 0.85 0.76 1"/>

      <body name="lower" pos="1.05 0 0">
        <joint name="elbow" type="hinge" axis="0 1 0"
               damping="0.18"/>
        <geom name="lower_link" type="capsule"
              fromto="0 0 0 0.78 0 0"
              size="0.058" mass="0.65"
              rgba="0.93 0.51 0.27 1"/>
        <geom name="effector" type="sphere"
              pos="0.78 0 0" size="0.075"
              mass="0.02" rgba="0.78 0.97 0.34 1"/>
      </body>
    </body>
  </worldbody>

  <actuator>
    <motor name="shoulder" joint="shoulder"
           ctrlrange="-14 14"/>
    <motor name="elbow" joint="elbow"
           ctrlrange="-14 14"/>
  </actuator>

  <keyframe>
    <key name="home" qpos="1.05 -1.35"/>
  </keyframe>
</mujoco>

models.name: Contact lab

changes.old: <!-- A contact-rich drop test. Tune restitution, observe rebound. -->
changes.replacement: <!-- Recovered drop test: inspect contact response using solref. -->
changes.reason: Describe the actual MuJoCo contact parameter.
Replace the unsupported geom restitution attribute with an explicit time-constant/damping-ratio baseline. This is not a conversion of coefficient of restitution 0.45.

remaining_caveats: The solref baseline does not preserve or promise the old JavaScript bounce coefficient. Contact behavior must be measured in the real engine.

The original tiny central imu site is preserved. Its touch sensor does not cover the floor-contact surface and should not be treated as a reliable contact detector; use data.ncon or a properly placed/enlarged site.
models.original_xml:
<mujoco model="drop_test">
  <!-- A contact-rich drop test. Tune restitution, observe rebound. -->
  <option gravity="0 0 -9.81"
          timestep="0.002" integrator="implicitfast"/>

  <worldbody>
    <light pos="1 3 3" dir="-1 -1 -1" directional="true"/>
    <geom name="floor" type="plane" size="5 5 0.1"
          rgba="0.35 0.37 0.32 1"/>

    <body name="body" pos="0 0 2.20">
      <freejoint name="root"/>
      <geom name="box" type="box" size="0.18 0.18 0.18"
            mass="0.80"
            restitution="0.45"
            rgba="0.88 0.85 0.76 1"/>
      <site name="imu" pos="0 0 0" size="0.02"
            rgba="0.78 0.97 0.34 1"/>
    </body>
  </worldbody>

  <sensor>
    <framepos name="body_pos" objtype="body" objname="body"/>
    <framelinvel name="body_vel" objtype="body" objname="body"/>
    <touch name="floor_contact" site="imu"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>
